sources.citation: Wagiman online dictionary site prose pages ( 'The sounds of Wagiman'), mirror saved 2026-08-17.
sources.note: Orthography and consonant/vowel description only; zero occurrences of stress/accent/prosody.

sources.citation: Krauße, Daniel. 2021. Towards a theory of complex predicates in Australian and Oceanic languages: an analysis of coverb constructions in Wagiman and serial verb constructions in Vurës. PhD thesis, University of Newcastle (NSW). xix+365 pp. (figshare/openresearch.newcastle.edu.au record 28971980)
sources.note: Sec. 5.2 'Phonology and orthography' (p.148ff) gives phoneme inventory, phonotactics, -Ma allomorphy, vowel harmony, glottal-stop epenthesis; no word-stress placement statement anywhere (grep of full text: 'stress' only in an unrelated Vurës article remark). p.148: 'No detailed study of the Wagiman phonology has been published to date. As part of his grammar, Cook (1987:24-65) provides a brief analysis of the phoneme inventory, prosody and glottal stop features in Wagiman.' -- locates the prosody description in Cook 1987.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 1974. Daly Family languages, Australia. Pacific Linguistics C-32. Canberra: ANU. (text layer on file from another audit folder)
sources.note: Checked table of contents and grep: Wageman/Wagiman is not among the languages treated (Tryon had by then excluded it from the Daly family); irrelevant for this key.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Wagiman language' (also de 'Wagiman', es 'Idioma wagiman'), API plaintext fetched sources 2026-09-17.
sources.note: No stress-placement statement; only 'It is not known, for instance, whether vowel harmony equally affects unstressed syllables.'

sources.citation: Wilson, Aidan. 2006. Negative evidence in linguistics: the case of Wagiman complex predicates. BA (Hons) thesis, University of Sydney. 80 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 2.1.2.1 'Phonology' (p.11) covers only coverb-final consonants and the phonemic glottal stop; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wilson, Stephen & Mark Harvey. 2001. The Wagiman online dictionary -- IPA version of the dictionary pages (11 letter files, 1385 transcriptions).
sources.note: Transcriptions are in SIL-IPA93 legacy encoding; a byte census finds no stress-mark code points (0xC8/0xC7 absent) -- no stress is marked on any headword. The site's prose section 'The sounds of Wagiman' (2026-08 mirror at ling/synchro/tropics/audit422/round2/sources/wagiman_dict_site/) is orthography + segment inventory only, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Austin, Peter. 1988. Phonological voicing contrasts in Australian Aboriginal languages. La Trobe Working Papers in Linguistics 1. (Wayback capture, truncated at archive time: 130617 of 155221 bytes; content streams recovered to)
sources.note: Mentions Wagiman only for the stop-voicing contrast ('Cook (1987:35) argues that in Wagiman it is voicing which is the consistent auditory cue for the stop contrast'); the 'stressed (i.e. first) vowel' remark in this paper concerns Bularnu (Breen 1974), not Wagiman. No Wagiman stress statement.

sources.note: Open Library snippet of sec. 2: '2. PHONOLOGY The phonemes of Wageman are as follow: Consonants Bilabial Alveolar Alv-palatal Velar... continuants r Vowels i u a 3. NOUNS There are no noun classes in Wageman...' -- a bare phoneme chart, no stress statement. (An initial-stress rule found in the same volume -- 'primary stress falls on the initial syllable and secondary stress falls on following alternate syllables' -- belongs to Hughes & Leeding's 'The phonemes of Nunggubuyu', not to the Wageman paper; its example words are Nunggubuyu, e.g. yagi 'not'.)
